newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Third Indonesian activist jailed for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Third Indonesian activist jailed for subversion.

text.p: A third Indonesian activist from the unrecognised People's Democratic Party (PRD) has been jailed for four years for subversion, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.

The newspaper said judges in the Surabaya State Court in East Java on Wednesday sentenced Mochamad Soleh, 25, making him the third PRD activist jailed on subversion charges this week for manipulating, undermining and deviating from state policy.
The prosecutor had sought a five-year sentence for the charges, which carry a maximum penalty of death.
On Tuesday, the same court in Indonesia's second-largest city sentenced Dita Indah Sari, 30, to six years in jail and Coen Husein Pontoh, 27, to four years on subversion charges.
The three activists had all been accused of helping to organise a labour strike and demonstration in Surabaya last July in which more than 10,000 workers from 10 factories took part.

"The council of judges should not be taken seriously. I am not guilty and I reject this verdict," the newspaper quoted Soleh, who was wearing a red headband reading "Democracy or Death", as shouting after the verdict was pronounced.
Another 11 PRD activists are being tried in Jakarta on subversion charges.
Indonesia recognises only three political parties, dominated by the ruling Golkar party.
